title: Service stability: experiments roadmap, stakeholder schedule, and handoff plan (Q2 2026)
content:
Purpose:
This working plan captures a set of small, measurable experiments and the cross-functional cadence needed to improve service stability and validate SLO choices for the next two quarters. It focuses on low-risk experiments that provide high signal for SLO definition, alert tuning, and operational handoff.

Scope:
- Services: API ingress, model-serving pods, KV-cache layer, and the routing/fallback paths used in Hosted and Dedicated modes.
- Teams: SRE, Serving Runtime, Platform, Product (Hosted API), Observability, Solutions Engineering.
- Outcomes: concrete measurement changes, updated runbooks, and a canary rollout playbook for SLO-based policy changes.

Background / Rationale:
We have broad agreement to tighten latency and availability SLOs for key routes, but limited production evidence on tail behavior with proposed batching and cache strategies. Rather than a big-bang SLO change, we will run targeted experiments to gather signal, adjust alerts, and automate safe rollouts.

High-level objectives:
1) Surface high-quality signals that disambiguate platform vs model-caused latency/failures.
2) Reduce repeat incidents caused by alert noise by 30% in Q3 relative to Q1.
3) Produce a validated SLO tuning cookbook and automated canary that can be applied to 3 representative routes by end of Q3.

Success metrics (for the program):
- Experiment signal-to-noise: > 70% of experiments produce a clear next action (tune threshold, change retry policy, revert config).
- Alert noise reduction: 30% fewer on-call alerts attributable to known noisy signals after dedup/tuning follow-ups.
- Runbook coverage: 100% of the three pilot routes have updated runbooks and an automated runbook test.

Experiment catalog (short descriptions and owner):
1) KV-cache prefix priming (owner: Marcus Lin)
   - Goal: Measure tail latency reduction for long-conversation traffic when prefix cache is warmed.
   - Variant A: proactive priming for top 10% prefixes from historical sessions.
   - Variant B: reactive priming with delayed prefetch (100ms window).
   - Measurement: p50/p95/p99 latency for same-session tokens, cache hit ratio, additional compute cost.

2) Conservative batching threshold experiment (owner: Evelyn Cho)
   - Goal: Quantify latency vs cost tradeoff of increasing batch windows by 10/20/50ms.
   - Design: Randomized sampling by request route, with fallback to baseline on latency spike.
   - Measurement: per-token cost, p99 latency, error rate during bursts.

3) Graceful fallback stress test (owner: Diego Ramirez)
   - Goal: Validate end-to-end fallback to smaller model variants under synthetic load and measure user-visible degradation.
   - Design: Gradual load injection to trigger routing policy switch; measure successful failovers and downstream errors.
   - Measurement: failover success %, time-to-failover, user-perceived quality score (synthetic metric).

4) Alert dedup canvas and threshold sweep (owner: Sofia Nguyen)
   - Goal: Reduce noisy SLO alerts by grouping signals and sweeping thresholds to find operating sweet spots.
   - Design: Offline replay + small-scale live experiments that only change alert rules (no infra changes).
   - Measurement: duplicate-alert ratio, mean time to acknowledge (MTTA), on-call noise taxonomy.

Measurement plan and dashboards:
- Each experiment must ship an instrumentation checklist: metric names, aggregation windows, tagging keys, and required dashboards.
- Observability will create experiment dashboards under /dashboards/stability-experiments/<experiment-name>. Required panels: latency histograms, error breakdown by component, cache hit/miss, routing traffic split.
- Baseline capture window: 7 days prior to experiment start. Experiment window: 72 hours minimum, extendable to 7 days for low-frequency signals.
- Postmortem signal: every experiment includes a 48-hour, lightweight writeup with recommended next actions (tune, rollback, escalate, product decision).

Stakeholder schedule (bi-weekly cadence across Q2):
- Week 0 (Feb 16): Alignment sync — SRE + Product + Serving Runtime: finalize experiment list and owners. (Owner: Anya)
- Week 1 (Feb 23): Instrumentation readiness check — Observability signoff, dashboards scaffolded. (Owner: Sofia)
- Week 2 (Mar 2): Experiment kickoff — launch KV-cache priming and alert dedup canvas. (Owners: Marcus, Sofia)
- Week 4 (Mar 16): Mid-experiment review — preliminary signals and decisions. (Owners: experiment leads)
- Week 6 (Mar 30): Launch batching threshold experiment. (Owner: Evelyn)
- Week 8 (Apr 13): Canary failover stress test kickoff. (Owner: Diego)
- Week 10 (Apr 27): Rollup retrospective — recommended SLO/alert changes and runbook updates. (Owner: Anya)
- Handoff milestone (May 11): Deliver automated canary playbook + runbooks for 3 pilot routes to Platform and Product. (Owner: Priya)

Communication plan (audiences, channels, templates):
- Audience: Oncall SREs, Platform engineers, Product owners for the affected routes, Support triage leads.
- Channels: #sre-stability Slack for live updates, Confluence for experiment writeups, Weekly stability working sync (calendar invite), and a one-off town hall for broader engineering.
- Templates: Short experiment kickoff note (what, why, metric owners, rollback triggers), daily signal summary (for active experiments), final recommendation memo. Templates live in linked_artifacts Confluence page.

Rollout, handoff, and runbook checklist (required for completion):
- Instrumentation validated: metrics and dashboards pass smoke tests.
- Playbook steps automated where possible (canary switch, traffic cutover, rollback).
- Runbook updated: triage steps, common remediation commands, post-incident checklist.
- Post-experiment A/B decision recorded and assigned to a product owner for implementation.
- Handoff meeting scheduled and recorded with action items and owners.

Escalation and rollback triggers (examples):
- If p99 latency increases by > 50% relative to baseline for 10 minutes AND error rate > 0.5% for the same window, auto-rollback batching change.
- If failover results in unsuccessful return-to-normal within 5 minutes for >30% of requests, trigger platform on-call and revert routing policy.
- Any experiment causing customer-facing HTTP 5xx increase > 0.2% triggers immediate pause and on-call paging.

Dependencies and constraints:
- Observability capacity: dedicated dashboard and metric retention changes for experiment signal — must be approved by Observability team before Week 1.
- Serving Runtime feature flags: need a short-lived flagging mechanism for batching window changes and KV priming toggles.
- Test accounts and synthetic traffic generator for failover validation.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: experiments are underpowered due to low traffic on some routes. Mitigation: sample-based experiments across routes and extended windows.
- Risk: too many concurrent experiments cause signal interference. Mitigation: limit parallel experiments to two per service and coordinate schedule.
- Risk: on-call fatigue from extra alerts. Mitigation: default to analysis-first (offline) for threshold sweeps and use simulated alerts for training.

Decisions needed (by Feb 20):
- Approve the initial experiment list and owners.
- Confirm Observability capacity for dedicated dashboards and retention.
- Allocate synthetic traffic budget for failover stress tests.

Next steps (immediate):
- Anya to host alignment sync (Week 0) and capture final owners.
- Observability to scaffold dashboard templates and validation checklist.
- Experiment leads to fill the instrumentation checklist and schedule smoke-run with Observability.

Appendix: quick templates (short forms)
- Kickoff note (two-line summary + primary metric + rollback trigger + owner contact)
- Daily signal summary (what changed vs baseline, one-sentence interpretation, recommended 1 action)
- Post-experiment memo (background, data captured, recommendation, required follow-ups)

Notes to readers: this is an iterative working document. Add experiment updates and short postmortems to the Confluence page linked above. Expect the schedule to slide +/-1 week as we tune instrumentation and react to early signals.
